title: Fixed-base critical-degree injectivity and cokernel monotonicity
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $p:X\to S$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and $q\in\mathbf Z$ with $q\ge1$. Assume $\mathrm{BC}(p,\Lambda,q-1)$ in the fixed-base, single-degree sense of [sk-def-bc]. Let $g:T\to S$ be quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and let $e:Y=X\times_ST\to T$ and $h:Y\to X$ be the projections [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. For a sheaf $M$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], write $b_M:p^{-1}R^qg_*M\to R^qh_*e^{-1}M$ for the canonical base-change map [sk-def-bc, def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Then (1) $b_M$ is a monomorphism for every $M$; (2) for every monomorphism $u:M\hookrightarrow N$ of such sheaves, the map $\operatorname{Coker}(b_M)\to\operatorname{Coker}(b_N)$ induced by naturality of the base-change map in $u$ is a monomorphism. Cokernels and monomorphisms are taken in the abelian categories of $\Lambda$-module sheaves [def-sp-abelian]. No universal base-change, annihilator, or invertibility hypothesis is imposed.
